question: Sapna invested ₹21,900 at simple interest, partly at 14% per annum and partly at 10% per annum. If she receives the same interest on both investments after 2 years, find the amount (in ₹) invested at 14% per annum.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interest and Time are equal for two investments, the principal is distributed in the inverse ratio of their rates.

Ratio of Principal (P₁ : P₂) = R₂ : R₁ = 10 : 14 = 5 : 7.

Total ratio parts = 5 + 7 = 12.

Amount invested at 14% (P₁) = (5 ÷ 12) × 21900 = 5 × 1825 = 9125.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,125.**
